title: Subsets
statement: You get a list of different integers. Return every possible subset: any selection of the numbers, including none of them and all of them. The result must not repeat a subset. The subsets can come back in any order.

example.caption: Three numbers give 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 subsets, from the empty one to all three.

idea.sentence: Walk through the numbers and, for each one, branch twice: take it, or leave it out. Every full walk is one subset, and you undo each choice to try the other.

jargon.plain: Make a choice, explore everything that follows, then undo the choice and make the other one.
A tree where each level is one yes or no question. Every leaf is one finished answer.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of different numbers, e.g. [1,2,3] (keep it to 3 or 4)

compare.bruteLabel: Bitmask: write each number 0 to 2^n as bits
compare.unit: subsets built (it doubles with every extra number, so 2^n is the closest shape)

rows.name: Bitmask loop
rows.note: Count from 0 to 2^n - 1. Each bit says whether that number is in the subset. No recursion, same output size.

rows.name: Take or leave
rows.note: There are 2^n leaves. Copying each subset costs up to n. Space is the recursion depth, not counting the output.

fast.takeaway: The answer itself has 2^n subsets, so nothing can beat that. The point is a clean way to visit each subset exactly once.

stages.title: Start empty
stages.note: path holds the numbers taken so far. It works like a stack: push to take, pop to undo.

stages.title: Take it
stages.note: Push nums[i] on the path and decide the next number.

stages.title: Undo, then leave it
stages.note: Pop nums[i] so the path is as before, then decide the next number without it.

stages.title: Record
stages.note: When every number has been decided, the path is one subset. Save a copy of it.

edges.title: Empty input
edges.why: There is exactly one subset of nothing: the empty one. The walk has no decisions, so it records the empty path once.

edges.title: One number
edges.why: One decision, two leaves. Leave it gives [], take it gives [5].

edges.title: Negatives and zero
edges.why: Values play no part in the walk. Only positions matter, so negatives and zero need no special case.

edges.title: Count doubles
edges.why: Each extra number doubles the leaves. That is why the input is kept tiny.

gotchas.text: Push [...path], not path. Pushing the array stores a reference, and the later pops would empty every saved subset.
Save append([]int{}, path...). Appending path itself, or a reslice of it, shares one backing array, so saved subsets change as the search goes on. This is the classic Go backtracking bug.
append([]int(nil), path...) copies too, but gives nil for the empty path. That marshals to null, not []. Use []int{} as the seed so the empty subset stays an empty list.
Do the pop on every path that did a push. The undo is what lets the second branch start from the same path as the first.
The empty subset and the full set both count. They are the first and last leaves of the walk.

recap.key: For each number, push it and recurse, then pop and recurse again. At the end, save a copy of the path.
recap.complexity: Time O(n · 2ⁿ). Space O(n) for the recursion, plus the output.
moves: Keep a path and an index i
Take: push nums[i], recurse on i + 1
Leave: pop, recurse on i + 1 again
At i == n save a copy of the path
